findings.description: The EBS volume attached to the portal server does not set encrypted = true (nor a KMS key), so data written to this additional disk is stored unencrypted. Any snapshot or underlying storage exposure would reveal cleartext data.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true means every instance launched in this subnet automatically receives a public IP. Combined with the route table's 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway, workloads such as aws_instance.portal_server are directly reachable from the internet without an explicit decision.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true auto-assigns public IPs to all instances in this subnet, which is also associated with a route table containing a default route to the internet gateway, placing any workload directly on the public internet.

A 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway is applied to the route table associated with both subnets, making every subnet public and removing any network segmentation between the portal workloads and the internet.

The EC2 user_data script exports static AWS access key and secret key values in cleartext. User data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by anyone with access to the instance (including via SSRF), leaking long-lived IAM credentials.
No root_block_device or ebs_block_device encryption settings are specified, so the instance's root volume may be stored unencrypted at rest.
No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled; combined with a public-facing web server this allows SSRF-based theft of instance metadata and credentials.
The instance serves content over plain HTTP (apache2 on port 80 with no TLS configuration), so all portal traffic traverses the internet unencrypted.
Port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access on the portal server to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing an unencrypted HTTP service to the whole internet with no load balancer or WAF boundary in front of it.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained outbound channel for data exfiltration or command-and-control if the instance is compromised.
The VPC flow log archive bucket defines no server-side encryption configuration, leaving sensitive network telemetry stored without enforced encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or ACL/policy controls are configured for the flow log bucket, so nothing prevents a public ACL or bucket policy from exposing network log data.
The bucket has no policy requiring aws:SecureTransport, permitting flow log data to be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.
force_destroy = true allows the flow log bucket and all stored network audit records to be deleted without emptying it first, undermining integrity and retention of security evidence.

The EBS snapshot is created from aws_ebs_volume.portal_server_disk with no encryption explicitly configured or verified; if the source volume is unencrypted the snapshot stores the portal server's disk data in cleartext, and snapshots are a common vector for data exfiltration if shared or copied.

The network interface is attached to the public-facing portal subnet but declares no security_groups attribute, so it receives the VPC default security group rather than the restricted aws_security_group.portal_sg, weakening the intended network boundary for the interface.
